m1_yoy.name: M1 growth
m1_yoy.read: Narrow money held largely by corporates. Accelerating M1 means cash is moving into transaction balances — firms are paying, restocking and investing rather than parking money in term deposits.

implications.growth: Classic 2-3 quarter leading indicator of nominal activity, industrial profits and PPI. A sustained M1 upturn is the single best confirmation that easing is reaching corporate balance sheets.
implications.inflation: Leads PPI more reliably than CPI in China. Persistent sub-zero M1 is a deflation warning.
implications.policy: Weak M1 alongside adequate M2 tells the PBoC that liquidity is being supplied but not activated — argues for demand-side/fiscal action rather than more rate cuts.

m1_yoy.false_signals: Two large breaks: the 2024 crackdown on manual interest supplementation (手工补息) pushed corporate demand deposits out of M1 into wealth products, and the January 2025 redefinition added household demand deposits and non-bank payment institutions' client reserves. Pre- and post-2025 M1 are not the same aggregate — never read the level shift as an economic signal.

m2_yoy.name: M2 growth
m2_yoy.read: Broad money. Now largely a mirror of bank credit creation and government bond issuance rather than an independent policy target.

implications.growth: Weak direct read on growth. Its information content is mostly in the gap to nominal GDP growth — a widening positive gap means money is accumulating faster than it is being spent.
implications.inflation: The historical M2-to-inflation link has broken down; velocity has fallen persistently. Treat high M2 growth with deflation as evidence of a velocity/confidence problem, not latent inflation.
implications.policy: The PBoC formally de-emphasised M2/TSF quantity targets in the 2024 framework reform. A miss versus nominal GDP growth no longer mechanically triggers action.

m2_yoy.false_signals: Inflated by government bond issuance and by deposit migration between bank and non-bank channels. M2 can accelerate purely because wealth-management money returns to deposits, with no new credit created.

m1_m2_gap.name: M1 − M2 gap (scissors gap)
m1_m2_gap.read: The corporate animal-spirits gauge. Negative and widening means money is being created but sits idle in term deposits; positive and widening means it is being mobilised into transactions.

implications.growth: One of the better China-specific leading indicators for industrial profits and the inventory cycle, typically leading by 2-3 quarters.
implications.inflation: A sustained deeply negative gap is consistent with entrenched deflation — the hallmark of a balance-sheet recession where money is hoarded.
implications.policy: A deeply negative gap is the strongest quantitative argument that monetary transmission is impaired and that the binding constraint is demand, not supply, of credit.

m1_m2_gap.false_signals: Inherits both M1 breaks. The 2024-25 distortions mean the level of the gap is not comparable with pre-2024 history; watch the direction of change instead.

tsf_stock_yoy.name: Total social financing, stock
tsf_stock_yoy.name_zh: 社会融资规模存量同比
tsf_stock_yoy.read: The broadest measure of credit supplied to the real economy — bank loans plus bonds, shadow credit, equity and government bonds. The PBoC's preferred headline aggregate.

implications.growth: The level of TSF growth relative to nominal GDP growth defines whether leverage is rising or falling. Growth above nominal GDP growth means the economy is releveraging.
implications.inflation: Indirect. Works through the credit-to-demand channel with a long and currently unreliable lag.
implications.policy: The PBoC's stated aim is TSF growth 'broadly matching' nominal GDP growth. A sustained shortfall is the clearest official trigger for easing.

tsf_stock_yoy.false_signals: Increasingly driven by government bond issuance rather than private credit demand. Always decompose: TSF excluding government bonds is the true read on private-sector credit appetite. The LGFV debt swap (化债) also mechanically shrinks measured credit as hidden debt is refinanced into bonds.
tsf_stock_yoy.notes: Quarterly in this build: the only verified source is the quarterly PBoC Monetary Policy Report. The published series is monthly.

tsf_flow.name: TSF new flow
tsf_flow.read: Monthly gross new financing to the real economy. Highly seasonal — January is always the 'good start' (开门红) surge.

implications.growth: Only meaningful year-on-year or as a 12-month rolling sum. The composition matters more than the total.
implications.inflation: Minimal direct read.
implications.policy: Large downside surprises reliably precede policy support announcements.

tsf_flow.false_signals: Never compare month-on-month. Quarter-end and year-start window dressing, plus bill financing (票据融资) used to hit quotas, distort the monthly print.
tsf_flow.stateless: Strongly seasonal monthly flow. A z-score against unadjusted history conflates the seasonal pattern — the January 'good start' surge, quarter-end window dressing — with a genuine change in conditions. Judge it through the credit impulse, which is built from the 12-month rolling sum.

new_loans.name: New RMB loans
new_loans.read: The bank-credit core of TSF. The quality read is in the split: corporate medium-and-long-term loans signal genuine capex; bill financing signals quota-filling.

implications.growth: Corporate MLT loan growth is the component that maps to fixed asset investment. Household MLT loans map to the property cycle.
implications.inflation: Indirect, via demand.
implications.policy: A print dominated by bills tells the PBoC that banks cannot find borrowers — a signal that rate cuts alone will not work.

new_loans.false_signals: Bill financing surges flatter the headline while signalling the opposite of credit strength. Always strip bills before drawing a conclusion.
new_loans.stateless: Strongly seasonal monthly flow. A z-score against unadjusted history conflates the seasonal pattern — the January 'good start' surge, quarter-end window dressing — with a genuine change in conditions. Judge it through the credit impulse, which is built from the 12-month rolling sum.

credit_impulse.name: Credit impulse
credit_impulse.derived: 12m change in the 12m rolling flow of TSF, as % of nominal GDP
credit_impulse.read: The second derivative of credit — the change in the flow of new credit relative to GDP. It is the acceleration of credit, not its level, that moves activity.

implications.growth: The classic 2-3 quarter leading indicator for fixed asset investment, industrial production and commodity demand. Turning points matter more than levels.
implications.inflation: Historically a good lead on PPI and on global industrial commodity prices via China's investment cycle.
implications.policy: A negative impulse while growth targets are at risk is the standard precondition for a coordinated monetary-fiscal push.

credit_impulse.false_signals: The credit intensity of Chinese growth has fallen sharply — the same impulse now buys less activity than a decade ago. Government-bond-driven impulses transmit far more weakly than property-driven ones.
credit_impulse.basis_note: Scaled by the trailing 12-month credit flow, not nominal GDP, because no verified nominal GDP level series was available. Turning points are unaffected; the units are not comparable with a conventional percent-of-GDP credit impulse.

omo_7d.name: 7-day reverse repo rate (policy rate)
omo_7d.read: Since the June 2024 framework overhaul this is the PBoC's single primary policy rate. It anchors the money market and, via the LPR, the cost of credit.

implications.growth: The headline stance signal. Cuts are necessary but, given weak credit demand, far from sufficient.
implications.inflation: With deflation, a constant nominal policy rate means passively tightening real conditions.
implications.policy: This is now the rate to watch for the stance. The MLF rate has been demoted to a liquidity-provision tool.

omo_7d.false_signals: The nominal level badly understates tightness when the GDP deflator is negative. Always read alongside the real policy rate.

mlf_1y.name: 1-year MLF rate
mlf_1y.read: Formerly the medium-term policy anchor and the LPR reference. Explicitly demoted in 2024 to a pure liquidity-provision instrument priced by multi-price bidding.

implications.growth: Historical relevance only; no longer the stance signal.
implications.inflation: n/a
implications.policy: Still useful as the reference against which bank marginal funding (NCD rates) is judged.

mlf_1y.false_signals: Treating an MLF move as a stance change is now a category error. Watch the 7-day OMO rate instead.
mlf_1y.notes: Series ENDS March 2025 by construction. From that month's operation the PBoC moved the MLF to multiple-price bidding, so no single announced MLF rate exists thereafter. Forward-filling past this point invents a policy rate, and any spread computed against it is meaningless — which is why ncd_mlf_spread is expected to be unbuildable for recent periods.

lpr_1y.name: Loan prime rate, 1-year
lpr_1y.read: The benchmark for corporate working-capital lending, quoted monthly by 20 banks as a spread over the policy rate.

implications.growth: The direct pass-through channel to corporate borrowing costs.
implications.inflation: Indirect.
implications.policy: Pass-through is constrained by bank net interest margins, which are at historic lows — this is now the binding limit on how far the LPR can fall.

lpr_1y.false_signals: The quoted LPR understates actual easing — the weighted average lending rate has fallen further than the LPR as banks compete for scarce good borrowers.

lpr_5y.name: Loan prime rate, 5-year
lpr_5y.read: The mortgage and long-term investment benchmark — in practice the property policy rate.

implications.growth: The main monetary lever on the property cycle, which remains the dominant swing factor in Chinese domestic demand.
implications.inflation: Works on housing-related demand and, through the collateral channel, on household confidence.
implications.policy: Asymmetric 5-year cuts are the PBoC's standard way of easing property without easing broad credit.

lpr_5y.false_signals: Cuts do little when the constraint is expected house-price declines rather than the cost of finance — the real mortgage rate can rise even as the nominal LPR falls.

walr_general.name: Weighted average lending rate, general loans
walr_general.name_zh: 一般贷款加权平均利率
walr_general.read: The actual price the real economy pays for credit, from the PBoC Monetary Policy Report. The single truest measure of the cost of credit — better than any policy or benchmark rate.

implications.growth: The rate that actually enters firms' investment decisions.
implications.inflation: Deflated by the GDP deflator this is the key real cost-of-capital variable.
implications.policy: The PBoC cites this series as evidence of successful transmission. Its floor is set by bank margin viability.

walr_general.false_signals: Falling WALR can reflect a shift in the borrower mix toward state-owned and policy-favoured borrowers rather than genuine easing for the marginal private borrower.

real_policy_rate.name: Real policy rate (CPI-deflated)
real_policy_rate.read: The 7-day policy rate deflated by headline CPI. The stance as borrowers and savers actually experience it. A core-CPI version is also built where data allows; with core inflation near zero the two tell a similar story.

implications.growth: What matters for intertemporal decisions. A rising real rate tightens even as the nominal rate falls.
implications.inflation: Self-reinforcing: falling inflation raises the real rate, which suppresses demand and lowers inflation further — the debt-deflation trap.
implications.policy: The core argument for front-loaded, larger nominal cuts. Passivity is not neutrality when prices are falling.

real_policy_rate.false_signals: The choice of deflator changes the answer materially. Core CPI gives the mildest read, the GDP deflator the harshest. Show more than one.

real_lending_rate.name: Real lending rate (CPI-deflated)
real_lending_rate.read: The weighted average rate actually paid on general loans, deflated by consumer prices. The most policy-relevant cost-of-capital measure available. The GDP-deflator version is the theoretically preferred construction but is not built here — the December 2024 economic census revised the nominal GDP base, so a deflator spanning that break would be wrong.

implications.growth: Directly measures the burden on corporate borrowers. High and rising real lending rates with falling nominal rates is the signature of a debt-deflation dynamic.
implications.inflation: A high real rate suppresses investment and wages, reinforcing deflation.
implications.policy: The strongest quantitative case for decisive easing. Nominal cuts that merely track falling inflation deliver no easing at all.

real_lending_rate.false_signals: CPI understates China's deflation relative to the GDP deflator or PPI, so this series is the mildest of the three real-rate reads. Check the PPI-deflated version alongside it — for industrial borrowers that is the rate that bites.

rrr_large.name: Reserve requirement ratio, large banks
rrr_large.name_zh: 大型存款类机构存款准备金率
rrr_large.read: The share of deposits banks must hold at the PBoC. Cuts release permanent, zero-cost long-term liquidity — distinct from the temporary liquidity of OMOs.

implications.growth: Works by relieving the funding constraint and supporting bank margins rather than by lowering the price of credit.
implications.inflation: Minimal direct effect.
implications.policy: Highly visible signalling tool. The PBoC has indicated a practical floor around 5%, so the remaining room is finite and shrinking.

rrr_large.false_signals: A cut is often mistaken for a stance change. When credit demand is weak, released liquidity simply accumulates as excess reserves or flows into bonds.

usdcny.name: USD/CNY
usdcny.read: A higher print is a weaker renminbi, which loosens monetary conditions via net exports.

implications.growth: Depreciation supports the export channel, which has been the main offset to weak domestic demand.
implications.inflation: Imported inflation via commodities, but the pass-through to Chinese CPI is modest.
implications.policy: FX stability is a hard constraint. A weakening currency and a wide US-China rate differential limit how far the PBoC can cut without triggering outflows.

usdcny.false_signals: Bilateral USD/CNY conflates dollar strength with renminbi weakness. Judge the renminbi against the CFETS basket, not the dollar.
usdcny.notes: Trimmed to July 2005, the start of the managed float. Earlier history exists in the source but is not comparable: the rate was pegged at 8.28 for the decade before that, and was a dual-track administered rate before the 1994 unification. Including it would make the z-score measure a regime change rather than currency conditions.

cfets.name: CFETS RMB index
cfets.read: The trade-weighted renminbi against a basket of 25 currencies — the PBoC's own preferred measure and the true competitiveness signal.

implications.growth: A falling basket index is genuine loosening of external monetary conditions.
implications.inflation: The relevant channel for imported price pressure.
implications.policy: The PBoC manages the basket, not the dollar cross. Basket stability amid dollar strength implies tolerated bilateral depreciation.

cfets.false_signals: The basket can stay flat while the real effective exchange rate appreciates sharply, because China's deflation raises relative prices. In a deflation the REER is the binding measure. History is limited: CFETS serves only a rolling one-year window, so this series accumulates forward from first fetch and cannot be z-scored against a long history yet.

reer.name: Real effective exchange rate
reer.read: The trade-weighted renminbi adjusted for relative price levels — the true measure of external competitiveness and the FX component of any monetary conditions index.

implications.growth: The correct external-demand variable. REER appreciation tightens monetary conditions.
implications.inflation: Appreciation is disinflationary; in China's case it compounds domestic deflation.
implications.policy: REER depreciation via domestic deflation is the wrong kind of competitiveness gain — it signals the deflation problem rather than solving it.

reer.false_signals: Different providers (BIS broad vs narrow, IMF, Bruegel) give materially different levels. Be consistent about which series is used.

tsf_minus_ngdp.name: TSF growth − nominal GDP growth
tsf_minus_ngdp.name_zh: 社融增速与名义GDP增速之差
tsf_minus_ngdp.read: The PBoC's own stated benchmark: credit growth 'broadly matching' nominal GDP growth. The gap is the cleanest measure of whether the economy is releveraging or deleveraging.

implications.growth: A positive gap means debt is growing faster than the income available to service it. Sustained positive gaps in a deflation are how leverage ratios spiral.
implications.inflation: A persistent positive gap with no inflation is evidence that credit is financing balance-sheet repair and asset purchases rather than spending.
implications.policy: The ratio the PBoC watches to judge whether the quantity of credit is appropriate.

tsf_minus_ngdp.false_signals: Widens mechanically in a deflation even with no change in credit policy, because nominal GDP growth collapses. Decompose before concluding that credit policy has loosened.

dr007.name: DR007
dr007.name_zh: 银行间存款类机构7天质押式回购利率
dr007.read: The weighted 7-day pledged repo rate among depository institutions only, against interest-rate-bond collateral. The PBoC's designated benchmark from 2016 until the 2026 shift to the overnight tenor, because it strips out credit and collateral-quality noise.

implications.growth: No direct read on growth. It measures the cost of settlement balances, not the cost of credit.
implications.inflation: None directly.
implications.policy: The operational target. The PBoC steers DR007 around the 7-day OMO rate; persistent deviation is the clearest statement of operational intent.

dr007.false_signals: A very low DR007 is routinely misread as aggressive easing. It just as often reflects weak credit demand — banks cannot lend, so reserves pile up and the money market clears cheap. Loose money market, tight credit is the defining Chinese configuration.

dr007_omo_spread.name: DR007 − 7d OMO spread
dr007_omo_spread.read: The deviation of actual bank funding costs from the policy rate the PBoC is targeting. The workhorse China liquidity gauge for a decade — but note that the Q1 2026 Monetary Policy Report moved the declared operating anchor to the OVERNIGHT tenor, so from 2026 the policy-relevant deviation is DR001 − policy rate, bounded at ±25bp. Track both; weight DR001 from 2026 forward.

implications.growth: None directly, but a persistently negative spread signals that liquidity is not being absorbed by credit creation.
implications.inflation: None.
implications.policy: Negative and widening means the PBoC is supplying more than the system needs, or credit demand is absent. Positive and widening means deliberate restraint or a funding squeeze. Still the best long history available, but it is no longer the series the PBoC is steering.

dr007_omo_spread.false_signals: Quarter-ends, tax payment weeks and the Chinese New Year cash drain produce mechanical spikes that carry no policy information. Judge the spread on its 20-day average, not the daily print.

r007.name: R007
r007.name_zh: 银行间7天质押式回购利率(全市场)
r007.read: The all-market 7-day repo rate, including non-bank financial institutions and lower-quality collateral.

implications.growth: None directly.
implications.inflation: None.
implications.policy: Useful only in combination with DR007 — the gap is the informative part.

r007.false_signals: R007 spikes can reflect a single stressed non-bank borrower rather than system-wide conditions.

r_dr_spread.name: R007 − DR007 spread
r_dr_spread.read: The premium non-banks pay over banks for the same tenor. A direct measure of funding stratification — whether liquidity is reaching beyond the large banks.

implications.growth: None directly.
implications.inflation: None.
implications.policy: A widening gap signals stress at the non-bank periphery and leverage unwinding. It is the early-warning indicator for bond-market deleveraging episodes and the one to watch for financial stability risk.

r_dr_spread.false_signals: Quarter-end MPA assessment mechanically widens the spread as banks withdraw from lending to non-banks. Strip quarter-end dates before interpreting.

ncd_1y_aaa.name: 1-year AAA NCD rate
ncd_1y_aaa.read: The rate joint-stock banks pay for 1-year wholesale funding. The marginal cost of bank liabilities, and the best read on term funding pressure beyond overnight.

implications.growth: Indirect — bank funding costs set the floor under lending rates.
implications.inflation: None.
implications.policy: Rising NCD rates compress margins and limit how far banks can cut lending rates. The PBoC watches this as a transmission constraint.

ncd_1y_aaa.false_signals: Year-end and quarter-end regulatory ratios distort issuance and pricing. Also driven by government bond supply waves that force banks to fund inventory.

ncd_mlf_spread.name: 1y NCD − 1y MLF spread
ncd_mlf_spread.read: Whether banks can fund themselves in the market more cheaply than from the central bank. The classic gauge of bank liability pressure.

implications.growth: Indirect.
implications.inflation: None.
implications.policy: A positive spread means market funding is dearer than central bank funding — banks will take up MLF and the PBoC faces pressure to inject. A negative spread means ample liquidity and weak MLF demand.

ncd_mlf_spread.false_signals: Since the MLF's 2024 demotion to a liquidity tool with multi-price bidding, this spread is less of a policy signal and more a pure funding-pressure gauge.

excess_reserve_ratio.name: Excess reserve ratio
excess_reserve_ratio.read: Banks' voluntary reserves at the PBoC above the required minimum — the true buffer stock of system liquidity. Published quarterly in the Monetary Policy Report.

implications.growth: A high ratio alongside weak credit is direct evidence of a transmission blockage — the fuel is in the tank but the engine is not turning.
implications.inflation: None directly.
implications.policy: Roughly 1.5% is the conventional comfort threshold. Below that, funding markets turn fragile and the PBoC typically injects.

excess_reserve_ratio.false_signals: The structural downtrend reflects better liquidity management technology, not persistent tightening. Compare with the same quarter a year earlier, not with a decade ago.

net_injection_3m.name: PBoC net liquidity injection, 3m sum
net_injection_3m.read: Net central bank liquidity provision across all channels — open market reverse repos, MLF, outright reverse repos, PSL and government bond purchases, less maturities.

implications.growth: None directly; this is plumbing, not stance.
implications.inflation: None.
implications.policy: The clearest revealed preference of the PBoC's operational intent, especially when read against the calendar of bond supply and tax payments it is offsetting.

net_injection_3m.false_signals: Large gross injections often merely offset maturities, tax drains or bond issuance. Always judge net, and judge against what needed offsetting — a big injection in a heavy tax month is neutral, not loose.

outright_repo.name: Outright reverse repo operations
outright_repo.read: A tool introduced in October 2024 providing 3- and 6-month liquidity against outright-transferred collateral, filling the gap between short OMOs and 1-year MLF.

implications.growth: None directly.
implications.inflation: None.
implications.policy: Its creation signalled a deliberate shift away from MLF dependence and toward finer control of the medium-term funding curve. Rising reliance on it is part of the MLF's demotion.

outright_repo.false_signals: Short history — no cycle-tested behavioural norms yet. Interpret with caution.

fiscal_deposits.name: Government deposits at the PBoC, change
fiscal_deposits.read: Money moving between the banking system and the Treasury Single Account. A rise drains bank reserves; a fall injects them. Entirely outside the PBoC's control and one of the largest swing factors in Chinese liquidity.

implications.growth: A sustained build-up means fiscal money is being raised but not spent — a genuine drag on demand as well as liquidity.
implications.inflation: Indirect via fiscal impulse.
implications.policy: The PBoC's operations are largely designed to offset this. January, April, May, July and October are the heavy tax-drain months; December is the big spending release.

fiscal_deposits.false_signals: Purely seasonal in most months. Only the deviation from the seasonal norm carries information.

govt_bond_issuance.name: Government bond gross issuance
govt_bond_issuance.read: Central treasury plus local government bond issuance that the banking system has to absorb. GROSS, not net — redemptions are not in the source, so it overstates the reserve drain.

implications.growth: Positive for growth via the fiscal channel, negative for near-term bank liquidity — the two effects run in opposite directions and on different timescales.
implications.inflation: Supports demand and therefore prices, with a lag.
implications.policy: Heavy issuance windows reliably coincide with PBoC liquidity support; the central bank explicitly coordinates to prevent supply from tightening money markets.

govt_bond_issuance.false_signals: Boosts headline TSF without representing private credit demand. A TSF beat driven entirely by government bonds is not evidence of recovering credit appetite.

cgb_10y.name: 10-year CGB yield
cgb_10y.read: The benchmark long rate — jointly a growth-expectations, inflation-expectations and liquidity signal.

implications.growth: Falling yields in China have mostly signalled deteriorating nominal growth expectations rather than easy policy.
implications.inflation: The clearest market-based read on entrenched deflation expectations.
implications.policy: The PBoC has publicly resisted disorderly declines, warning on duration risk and one-way bets. Very low yields are therefore both a signal of and a constraint on policy.

cgb_10y.false_signals: A falling 10-year yield is not a loosening of monetary conditions — it is usually the market pricing a worse nominal growth path. Reading a bond rally as stimulus is the most common analytical error in Chinese macro.

cgb_1y.name: 1-year CGB yield
cgb_1y.read: The short end, tightly anchored to expected policy rates and money market conditions.

implications.growth: Minimal direct read.
implications.inflation: Minimal.
implications.policy: The market's expected path for the policy rate over the coming year. Trades below the OMO rate when cuts are expected.

cgb_1y.false_signals: Distorted by bank and money-fund demand for short collateral at quarter-ends.

term_spread.name: 10y − 1y CGB term spread
term_spread.read: The slope of the curve. Steepening normally signals recovering growth and inflation expectations; flattening signals the opposite or a duration-chasing squeeze.

implications.growth: A sustained steepening is one of the better market-based confirmations that reflation is taking hold.
implications.inflation: Embeds the market's inflation expectations, which in China are currently very low.
implications.policy: Extreme flatness alongside heavy long-end demand is what prompted PBoC verbal and operational intervention in the bond market.

term_spread.false_signals: In China the curve is heavily shaped by bank balance-sheet demand and regulatory treatment, so it is a noisier growth signal than in developed markets.

credit_spread_aa.name: 3y AA+ MTN spread over CGB
credit_spread_aa.read: The compensation demanded for corporate credit risk — the price of risk rather than the price of liquidity.

implications.growth: Widening spreads tighten financing conditions for the marginal private borrower ahead of any move in bank lending rates.
implications.inflation: None directly.
implications.policy: Sharp widening, especially in urban investment (城投) bonds, triggers targeted support rather than broad easing.

credit_spread_aa.false_signals: Implicit government support compresses spreads on quasi-sovereign issuers, so the series understates true credit risk. Spread compression can reflect an asset shortage (资产荒) rather than improving fundamentals.

cnh_hibor_on.name: Overnight CNH HIBOR
cnh_hibor_on.name_zh: 离岸人民币隔夜拆借利率
cnh_hibor_on.read: Offshore renminbi funding cost in Hong Kong. Spikes are the classic fingerprint of deliberate offshore liquidity tightening to squeeze short sellers.

implications.growth: None directly.
implications.inflation: None.
implications.policy: A sharp spike is an unambiguous signal of FX defence, and tells you the currency constraint is binding on domestic easing.

cnh_hibor_on.false_signals: Thin offshore market — spikes can be technical. Confirm against the CNH-CNY spread before concluding intervention.

shibor_3m.name: 3-month SHIBOR
shibor_3m.read: A quoted (not transacted) term rate. Retains relevance as a floating-rate benchmark but has lost ground to DR and NCD rates as a conditions gauge.

implications.growth: None directly.
implications.inflation: None.
implications.policy: Secondary confirmation of term funding pressure.

shibor_3m.false_signals: Quote-based and sticky — it can lag genuine moves in transacted funding costs.

cpi_yoy.name: CPI
cpi_yoy.name_zh: 居民消费价格指数同比
cpi_yoy.read: Headline consumer inflation. The deflator for the real policy rate and the clearest evidence on whether reflation is arriving.

implications.growth: Persistent near-zero or negative CPI signals demand deficiency rather than supply abundance.
implications.inflation: The target variable. China's implicit ~3% ceiling has not been a binding constraint for years; the risk is entirely on the downside.
implications.policy: Sub-target inflation is the primary justification for easing and the reason the real policy rate keeps drifting up absent nominal cuts.

cpi_yoy.false_signals: Heavily influenced by pork and fresh food. Always cross-check against core CPI, which strips food and energy.

core_cpi_yoy.name: Core CPI
core_cpi_yoy.read: CPI excluding food and energy — the underlying demand signal and the right deflator for the real policy rate.

implications.growth: The cleanest price-side read on domestic demand and the output gap.
implications.inflation: The series to watch for genuine reflation. A durable turn here is the confirmation that easing is working.
implications.policy: Sustained weak core CPI is the strongest technical case for further cuts.

core_cpi_yoy.false_signals: Services weights and administered prices (rents, utilities, healthcare) dampen the cyclical signal relative to other economies.
core_cpi_yoy.notes: Quarterly in this build; only a handful of observations were verifiable. The published series is monthly.

ppi_yoy.name: PPI
ppi_yoy.name_zh: 工业生产者出厂价格指数同比
ppi_yoy.read: Factory-gate prices. The key determinant of industrial profits and the price variable most sensitive to credit and the investment cycle.

implications.growth: Maps directly to industrial profits, which drive corporate capex and hiring. Prolonged PPI deflation squeezes the corporate sector's capacity to invest.
implications.inflation: The first place a credit-driven reflation shows up. Also China's main export of disinflation to the world.
implications.policy: Extended PPI deflation combined with excess capacity has pushed policy toward supply-side capacity discipline alongside demand support.

ppi_yoy.false_signals: Dominated by commodity base effects. Decompose into the production-materials versus consumer-goods components to read domestic demand.

gdp_deflator_yoy.name: GDP deflator
gdp_deflator_yoy.read: The economy-wide price level — the broadest and most honest measure of China's deflation, and the correct deflator for the real cost of credit.

implications.growth: Nominal GDP growth is what services debt. A negative deflator means the debt burden rises even when real growth hits target.
implications.inflation: The definitive deflation measure. Consecutive negative quarters mark economy-wide deflation regardless of what headline CPI shows.
implications.policy: The most powerful argument for aggressive nominal easing — and the variable the real-lending-rate calculation hinges on.

gdp_deflator_yoy.false_signals: Derived from nominal and real GDP, both revised. Quarterly and noisy; use a 4-quarter average for the underlying trend.
gdp_deflator_yoy.notes: Built from NBS quarterly GDP: cumulative nominal growth minus cumulative real growth, both legs from the same publisher and the same request, so the series does not straddle data vintages.

real_gdp_yoy.name: Real GDP, cumulative YTD
real_gdp_yoy.read: Official real growth, cumulative year-to-date — the form the NBS headlines. Resets each Q1.

implications.growth: The headline outcome against which policy is judged.
implications.inflation: The gap to potential drives price pressure.
implications.policy: Risk of missing the annual target is the single most reliable trigger for coordinated stimulus.

real_gdp_yoy.false_signals: Low volatility relative to underlying activity. Cross-check against nominal GDP, which tells the more honest story in a deflation.

nominal_gdp_yoy.name: Nominal GDP
nominal_gdp_yoy.read: Growth in current prices — what incomes, profits, tax revenue and debt service are actually measured in.

implications.growth: Nominal GDP growth falling below real GDP growth means the economy is in deflation and the debt-to-GDP ratio rises mechanically.
implications.inflation: The combined quantity-and-price outcome that monetary policy ultimately influences.
implications.policy: The benchmark the PBoC uses for 'credit growth broadly matching nominal GDP growth'. A widening gap between TSF growth and nominal GDP growth signals rising leverage without commensurate income.

nominal_gdp_yoy.false_signals: None material, but it receives far less attention than real GDP despite being the more policy-relevant series in a deflation.
nominal_gdp_yoy.notes: Cumulative year-to-date nominal growth, computed by comparing like year-to-date periods a year apart.

ncd_issuance_war.name: 3-month NCD issuance rate
ncd_issuance_war.read: The rate banks pay to issue 3-month negotiable certificates of deposit, from the PBoC Monetary Policy Report. A direct read on the marginal cost of short-term wholesale bank funding.

implications.growth: Indirect. Bank funding costs set the floor under lending rates, so a sustained rise limits how far loan pricing can fall.
implications.inflation: None directly.
implications.policy: Rising NCD costs compress net interest margins, which are the binding constraint on further LPR cuts. The PBoC watches this as a transmission limit.

ncd_issuance_war.false_signals: This is the 3-month point, not the 1-year AAA benchmark most strategists quote, and not an all-tenor average — the two sit at different levels and are not interchangeable. Quarter-end regulatory ratios distort issuance and pricing.

ncd_omo_spread.name: 3m NCD − policy rate spread
ncd_omo_spread.name_zh: 同业存单发行利率与政策利率利差
ncd_omo_spread.read: What banks pay for 3-month wholesale funding relative to the central bank's policy rate. The workable substitute for the conventional 1-year NCD versus MLF spread, now that the MLF has no single announced rate.

implications.growth: Indirect, via the cost and availability of bank credit.
implications.inflation: None directly.
implications.policy: A wide positive spread means market funding is dearer than central bank funding, so banks lean on PBoC facilities and pressure builds for injections. A narrow or negative spread signals genuinely ample liquidity.

ncd_omo_spread.false_signals: Compares a 3-month funding rate against a 7-day policy rate, so the level carries a structural term premium — read it as a change from its own history, not against zero.

m2_level.name: M2 stock
m2_level.read: The level of broad money. Useful mainly as the denominator for velocity and for scaling against nominal GDP.

implications.growth: The level says little; the growth rate and the ratio to nominal GDP carry the information.
implications.inflation: China's M2-to-GDP ratio is among the highest in the world without corresponding inflation — the clearest single piece of evidence that the quantity theory does not describe this economy.
implications.policy: Context for the PBoC's shift away from quantity targets.

m2_level.false_signals: A large and rising stock invites the inference that inflation must follow. It has not, for over a decade, because velocity has fallen as fast as the stock has grown.
m2_level.stateless: Trending level series. A z-score against its own history would read as permanently 'loose', because the level only ever rises — that says nothing about conditions. Read the growth rate instead.

tsf_stock_level.name: TSF stock
tsf_stock_level.read: The outstanding level of all financing to the real economy — the denominator for leverage ratios.

implications.growth: The ratio of this stock to nominal GDP is the macro leverage ratio, which constrains how much further credit-financed stimulus is possible.
implications.inflation: None directly.
implications.policy: The stock's growth rate against nominal GDP growth is the PBoC's stated benchmark for whether credit supply is appropriate.

tsf_stock_level.false_signals: Definitional expansions over time — local government special bonds, asset-backed securities and loan write-offs were added in 2018 — mean the long history is not a consistent series.
tsf_stock_level.stateless: Trending level series. A z-score against its own history would read as permanently 'loose', because the level only ever rises — that says nothing about conditions. Read the growth rate instead.

fx_reserves.name: FX reserves
fx_reserves.read: Official foreign exchange reserves. Historically the main channel through which balance-of-payments flows created domestic base money.

implications.growth: No direct read. Matters as a measure of the buffer available to defend the currency.
implications.inflation: Historically, reserve accumulation created base money and was sterilised through RRR increases — the reason China's RRR reached 21% in 2011.
implications.policy: Sharp declines signal capital outflow pressure and tighten the constraint on domestic easing. Stability around the $3.2trn mark has been a policy preference for years.

fx_reserves.false_signals: Monthly changes are dominated by valuation effects — dollar moves and bond price changes — rather than intervention. Never read a monthly change as intervention without adjusting for valuation.

rrr_small.name: Reserve requirement ratio, small and medium banks
rrr_small.name_zh: 中小型存款类机构存款准备金率
rrr_small.read: The reserve requirement for smaller banks, typically set 2 percentage points below the large-bank ratio, with additional targeted reductions for rural and small-business lenders.

implications.growth: Targeted cuts here are aimed at small and private enterprise credit, where the transmission blockage is most severe.
implications.inflation: Minimal direct effect.
implications.policy: The spread to the large-bank ratio shows how much of policy is structural and targeted rather than aggregate.

rrr_small.false_signals: The headline ratio understates actual easing for the smallest institutions, many of which already sit at the 5% floor and are unaffected by further cuts.

real_gdp_yoy_q.name: Real GDP, single quarter
real_gdp_yoy_q.read: Single-quarter rather than cumulative year-to-date growth — the cleaner read on quarterly momentum.

implications.growth: Turning points show up here a quarter or more before they appear in the cumulative series.
implications.inflation: The output gap implied by momentum drives price pressure.
implications.policy: Quarterly momentum against the annual target is what determines the urgency of stimulus.

real_gdp_yoy_q.false_signals: Noisier than the cumulative series and subject to revision.

nominal_gdp_level_cum.name: Nominal GDP, cumulative YTD
nominal_gdp_level_cum.read: Year-to-date nominal GDP in current prices. Resets each Q1, so the series is a sawtooth and must be differenced within a year before use.

implications.growth: Nominal GDP is what services debt and generates tax revenue — the honest measure of economic performance in a deflation.
implications.inflation: Nominal growth falling below real growth is the definition of economy-wide deflation.
implications.policy: The benchmark against which credit growth is judged.

nominal_gdp_level_cum.false_signals: The December 2024 economic census revised the 2023 base upward substantially, so growth rates computed across that break are wrong. This is precisely why no nominal GDP growth rate or GDP deflator is derived in this build.
nominal_gdp_level_cum.stateless: Cumulative year-to-date level that resets each Q1. A z-score on a sawtooth is meaningless.

real_lending_rate_ppi.name: Real lending rate (PPI-deflated)
real_lending_rate_ppi.read: The cost of credit deflated by factory-gate prices — the real borrowing cost faced by the industrial sector, which is where most corporate debt sits.

implications.growth: The single harshest and most relevant real-rate measure for Chinese manufacturing. With PPI deflation running for an extended period, industrial borrowers have faced double-digit real rates at times even as nominal rates fell to record lows.
implications.inflation: Self-reinforcing: high real rates suppress capex, worsening overcapacity and deepening PPI deflation.
implications.policy: The strongest quantitative argument that nominal easing has been insufficient. Closing this gap requires either far lower nominal rates or reflation of producer prices through capacity discipline and demand support.

real_lending_rate_ppi.false_signals: PPI is dominated by commodity base effects, so this series swings far more than the true cost of capital. Read the trend over several quarters, not a single print.

real_policy_rate_core.name: Real policy rate (core CPI)
real_policy_rate_core.name_zh: 实际政策利率(核心CPI平减)
real_policy_rate_core.read: The policy rate deflated by core CPI — the cleanest measure of the stance stripped of food and energy noise.

implications.growth: The right rate for intertemporal decisions once volatile components are removed.
implications.inflation: With core inflation near zero, holding the nominal rate constant means the real stance tightens passively.
implications.policy: The technically correct series for judging whether nominal cuts have delivered real easing.

real_policy_rate_core.false_signals: Only a handful of quarterly observations are available in this build, so the z-score is not meaningful. Treat as directional only.

cgb10y_omo_spread.name: 10y CGB − policy rate spread
cgb10y_omo_spread.read: How much term premium the long bond offers over the cost of funding it. The carry cushion available to leveraged bond positions.

implications.growth: A compressed spread reflects the market pricing a weak nominal growth path, not easy policy.
implications.inflation: Compression embeds falling inflation expectations.
implications.policy: A compressed spread combined with crowded overnight funding is the fragility configuration the PBoC warned about when it intervened verbally in the bond market and began selling duration. Below roughly 30bp there is almost no cushion against a funding shock.

cgb10y_omo_spread.false_signals: Reads as 'loose' when it widens, but widening can equally mean the market has lost confidence in the growth outlook at the long end. Always read alongside the level of the 10-year yield.

tsf_ex_govt_yoy.name: TSF excluding government bonds
tsf_ex_govt_yoy.name_zh: 社融(剔除政府债券)同比
tsf_ex_govt_yoy.read: Total social financing stripped of central and local government bond issuance — the true read on private-sector credit appetite.

implications.growth: The series that actually maps to private investment. Headline TSF has been carried by government bonds while this measure has kept decelerating.
implications.inflation: Private credit is the channel through which money becomes spending and therefore prices. Government bond issuance that funds debt swaps creates neither.
implications.policy: The gap between headline TSF and this series is the clearest evidence of whether stimulus is monetary or fiscal in substance.

tsf_ex_govt_yoy.false_signals: Requires a consistent government bond series to subtract; definitional changes to what counts as government financing break comparability across the 2018 revision.
tsf_ex_govt_yoy.derived: year-on-year change in the trailing 12m sum of tsf_ex_govt_flow

corp_mlt_loans_yoy.name: Corporate medium & long-term loans
corp_mlt_loans_yoy.read: Growth in the outstanding stock of corporate loans of maturity over one year — the credit that finances actual capital expenditure. 本外币 (local and foreign currency), read from section 一 of the PBoC's quarterly loan-direction report.

implications.growth: The highest-quality credit signal available: it maps directly to fixed asset investment and is immune to the bill-financing games that distort the monthly headline.
implications.inflation: Capex-driven credit is what eventually tightens capacity and lifts producer prices.
implications.policy: Sustained weakness here, alongside strong headline loans, tells the PBoC that banks are meeting quotas with short-dated paper rather than financing investment.

corp_mlt_loans_yoy.false_signals: Can be inflated by policy-directed lending to infrastructure and state-owned enterprises. Cross-check against private-sector fixed asset investment. Quarterly and released three to four weeks after quarter end, so it confirms a turn rather than calling one.

household_time_deposit_share.name: Household time-deposit share
household_time_deposit_share.read: The share of household deposits held in time rather than demand accounts — the 'termification' (定期化) gauge of precautionary saving.

implications.growth: A rising time share means households are hoarding rather than spending. It is the behavioural signature of a balance-sheet recession and the reason rate cuts have not lifted consumption.
implications.inflation: Directly measures the velocity collapse that has kept inflation near zero despite rapid money growth.
implications.policy: A falling time share would be the earliest credible evidence that confidence is returning and that easing is finally working through the household channel.

household_time_deposit_share.false_signals: Partly driven by the relative yield on deposits versus wealth-management products, so it moves on regulatory and rate-structure changes as well as on confidence.
household_time_deposit_share.unavailable: No machine-readable route to history. The 金融机构人民币信贷收支表 PDF does parse cleanly — 住户存款 / 活期存款 / 定期及其他存款 extract as text, twelve months to a file — but pbc.gov.cn exposes a node for the CURRENT year only: 2026ntjsj resolves, 2023/2024/2025 all 404, and the statistics hub carries no per-year links. A series from the one reachable file would be a single year, which is not enough to z-score.

overnight_repo_share.name: Overnight share of repo turnover
overnight_repo_share.read: The proportion of pledged repo volume transacted overnight. High readings mean the system is financing long positions with the shortest possible money.

implications.growth: None directly.
implications.inflation: None.
implications.policy: The purest gauge of crowded carry. Above roughly 88-90% the market is one bad funding day from a forced unwind, and the PBoC has historically leaned against liquidity at exactly these moments.

overnight_repo_share.false_signals: A high share looks like abundant liquidity and is recorded here as 'looser', but it is simultaneously a fragility signal. This is the one indicator where loose and dangerous are the same reading.
overnight_repo_share.unavailable: Not populated in this build — requires CFETS or exchange repo turnover microdata.

dr001.name: DR001
dr001.name_zh: 银行间存款类机构隔夜质押式回购利率
dr001.read: The overnight pledged repo rate among depository institutions. As of the Q1 2026 Monetary Policy Report this — not DR007 — is the PBoC's designated operating anchor, to be held within ±25bp of the 7-day policy rate.

implications.growth: None directly.
implications.inflation: None.
implications.policy: This is now the primary real-time read on whether the PBoC is delivering its intended stance. Because the band is explicit and narrow, a breach is a genuinely informative event rather than routine noise — which was never true of the old corridor.

dr001.false_signals: Overnight rates are the most sensitive to the daily settlement calendar, so single-day spikes around tax dates, quarter-ends and Chinese New Year carry no policy information. Read the 5-day average.
dr001.unavailable: Not populated in this build. Available daily from CFETS; this is the highest-priority series to add, since the 2026 framework makes it the operating target.

dr001_omo_spread.name: DR001 − policy rate spread
dr001_omo_spread.read: The deviation of the overnight anchor from the policy rate, against an explicit ±25bp band set in June 2026 when the corridor was narrowed from 70bp to 50bp.

implications.growth: None directly.
implications.inflation: None.
implications.policy: The successor to the DR007 spread as the headline liquidity gauge. Inside the band, policy is being delivered as intended; a sustained breach means the PBoC is either unable or unwilling to hold its own target, which is the single most informative liquidity event available.

dr001_omo_spread.false_signals: The band was only formalised in June 2026, so applying it to earlier history is anachronistic. Before 2026 the informative spread is DR007 − OMO.
dr001_omo_spread.unavailable: Not populated in this build — requires DR001.

tsf_swap_adjusted.name: TSF adjusted for the LGFV debt swap
tsf_swap_adjusted.read: Total social financing with the local-government hidden-debt swap programme stripped out. Swap bonds refinance existing obligations; they create no new spending power, but they inflate measured credit.

implications.growth: The adjusted series is what actually maps to demand. Unadjusted TSF will overstate the credit impulse for as long as the swap programme runs, which on current plans extends for several years.
implications.inflation: Refinancing generates no new spending and therefore no price pressure. Reading swap-inflated TSF as stimulus is how a forecaster ends up expecting reflation that does not arrive.
implications.policy: The PBoC and MoF both know the distinction; an external analyst who does not will systematically misjudge how much stimulus has actually been delivered.

tsf_swap_adjusted.false_signals: There is no official adjusted series — it must be constructed from the swap issuance calendar, so the adjustment is an estimate and different desks will get different numbers.
tsf_swap_adjusted.unavailable: Not populated in this build. Flagged by the literature scan as the single highest-value indicator to construct next: without it, measured stimulus is overstated for years.

r001.name: R001
r001.name_zh: 银行间隔夜质押式回购利率(全市场)
r001.read: The all-market overnight pledged repo rate, including non-banks. Paired with DR001 it gives the overnight equivalent of the R–DR stratification spread.

implications.growth: None directly.
implications.inflation: None.
implications.policy: The overnight R−DR gap is the fastest-moving read on whether liquidity is reaching beyond the large banks, and it moves before the 7-day gap does.

r001.false_signals: The most volatile rate on the board. Single-day spikes around tax dates, quarter-ends and Chinese New Year carry no policy information.

r_dr_spread_001.name: R001 − DR001 spread
r_dr_spread_001.read: Overnight funding stratification: what non-banks pay over banks for overnight money.

implications.growth: None directly.
implications.inflation: None.
implications.policy: The earliest warning of non-bank funding stress — it widens before the 7-day equivalent does.

r_dr_spread_001.false_signals: Quarter-end MPA assessment widens it mechanically as banks withdraw from lending to non-banks.

govt_deposits_level.name: Government deposits at the PBoC
govt_deposits_level.stateless: Trending level series — read the monthly change, which is what actually drains or adds bank reserves.
govt_deposits_level.read: The Treasury Single Account balance on the PBoC's balance sheet. Money sitting here is money withdrawn from the banking system.

implications.growth: A sustained build-up means fiscal revenue is being raised but not spent — a drag on demand as well as on liquidity.
implications.inflation: Indirect, via the fiscal impulse.
implications.policy: The PBoC's daily operations are largely designed to offset moves in this account.

govt_deposits_level.false_signals: Dominated by the tax calendar. Only the deviation from the seasonal norm carries information.

pboc_claims_odc.name: PBoC claims on banks
pboc_claims_odc.name_zh: 对其他存款性公司债权
pboc_claims_odc.stateless: Trending level series — the change is the signal, not the level.
pboc_claims_odc.read: The stock of all PBoC lending to banks: open market operations, MLF, PSL and outright reverse repo combined. Changes in this stock ARE net liquidity injection.

implications.growth: None directly — this is plumbing, not stance.
implications.inflation: None.
implications.policy: Far more robust than summing daily operation announcements, because it captures every facility at once and cannot miss one.

pboc_claims_odc.false_signals: Rising claims can reflect banks rolling maturing facilities rather than new support. Judge the change against what needed offsetting — bond supply, tax drains — not against zero.

tsf_ex_govt_flow.name: TSF excluding government bonds, flow
tsf_ex_govt_flow.name_zh: 社融(剔除政府债券)增量
tsf_ex_govt_flow.stateless: Strongly seasonal monthly flow — judge it through the year-on-year series rather than the monthly print.
tsf_ex_govt_flow.read: The sum of every non-government financing component the PBoC breaks out — the monthly flow of private-sector credit.

implications.growth: This is the series that maps to private investment; headline TSF has been carried by government bonds while this decelerated.
implications.inflation: Private credit is how money becomes spending. Government bonds funding debt swaps create neither.
implications.policy: The gap to headline TSF shows whether stimulus is monetary or fiscal in substance.

tsf_ex_govt_flow.false_signals: A construction, not a published series: small components outside the published breakdown (ABS, loan write-offs) are excluded, so it is slightly below a true TSF-minus-government-bonds.

cgb_3y.name: 3-year CGB yield
cgb_3y.read: The 3-year point of the government curve — the risk-free benchmark for the 3-year credit spread.

implications.growth: Minimal direct read.
implications.inflation: Minimal.
implications.policy: Sits between the policy-anchored short end and the growth-expectations long end.

cgb_3y.false_signals: Distorted by bank demand at quarter-ends.

mtn_aa_3y.name: 3-year AA+ medium-term note yield
mtn_aa_3y.read: The yield on 3-year AA+ medium-term notes — the cost of market funding for a decent but not top-tier corporate borrower.

implications.growth: Rising yields tighten financing for the marginal private borrower before bank lending rates move.
implications.inflation: None directly.
implications.policy: Sharp rises, especially in urban investment paper, trigger targeted support rather than broad easing.

mtn_aa_3y.false_signals: Implicit government support compresses quasi-sovereign spreads, so the level understates true credit risk.

corp_mlt_loans_level.name: Corporate medium & long-term loans, balance
corp_mlt_loans_level.name_zh: 企事业单位中长期贷款余额
corp_mlt_loans_level.read: Outstanding stock of corporate medium and long-term loans. Carried as the level the growth rate is computed from, so the two can be reconciled against the published report.

implications.growth: Read the growth rate, not the level — the stock rises almost monotonically.
implications.inflation: No direct read from the level.
implications.policy: Useful only to audit the year-on-year figure against the source.

corp_mlt_loans_level.false_signals: Can be inflated by policy-directed lending to infrastructure and state-owned enterprises. Cross-check against private-sector fixed asset investment. Quarterly and released three to four weeks after quarter end, so it confirms a turn rather than calling one.
